meta.order: Character frequency rank (Jun Da Modern Chinese list, via hanziDB).

fields.hsk_level: HSK 3.0 character level (1-6; 7 means band 7-9; null if not in the syllabus).
fields.supplement: Same card format: the HSK 3.0 level 1-6 characters that fall outside the frequency top 2,000 (mostly everyday-life vocabulary that is rare in written corpora). rank is their true frequency rank.
fields.gloss: One-line summary of the character (Unihan). Use as a quick reminder; the per-reading definitions are more precise.
fields.readings: One entry per pronunciation worth knowing, most important first. Rare and literary readings are omitted.
fields.readings[].bound_form: true when the character with this reading is not used as a standalone word. A "(bound form)" prefix on a single sense means only that sense is bound.
fields.readings[].patterns: Hand-written usage patterns with an example (grammar characters, measure words, some standalone verbs).
fields.readings[].words: Common words using the character with this reading, most useful first.
fields.words[].zipf: Word frequency on the Zipf scale: 6 = extremely common, 5 = very common, 4 = common, 3 = occasional.
fields.words[].hsk: HSK 3.0 level (1-6; 7 means band 7-9). Absent when the word is not on the HSK lists.
fields.words[].max_partner_rank: Highest frequency rank among the other characters in the word; null if any is outside the top 2,000. A word is fully readable once you have studied cards up to this rank.
